title: The All Time Ballon d’Or Table: Ranking the 35 Most Successful Players
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey WhitebloomOct 22, 2026Lionel Messi has won more Ballon d’Or trophies than any other player. / FRANCK FIFE/AFP/Getty ImagesThe Ballon d’Or was not supposed to get this big.

One of the brains behind the creation of a prize given to the best soccer player of the year, Jacques Ferran, admitted: “The Ballon d’Or, at first, was just another trophy.” His successor as France Football director Pascal Ferré claimed that it was a concept “born with the carefree spirit of a one-night stand.”

The award has since spiraled beyond any of their possible conceptions into a hulking behemoth which players freely and openly crave. It may have taken on a new form but the goal has always been the same for the panel of jurors given a vote: objectively choose the best player across the previous 12 months.

Taken in isolation, some of the results can appear odd. But there is an argument that the Ballon d’Or should be viewed as one continuous judgement of talent rather than a discrete series of prizes. Rather than looking at a single dot of a pointillism painting, it’s worth taking a few steps back to admire the whole piece in all its majesty. This is the idea of the all-time Ballon d’Or table.
When Did the Ballon d’Or Get So Big?. dark. Next. Ballon d’Or feature

This is no perfect list. The prize could only be won by Europeans until 1995, which is why you won’t find the names of Pelé or Diego Maradona anywhere. But the archive of Ballon d’Or voting which spans 70 years is one of the most comprehensive catalogues of tangible, contemporaneous and obsessively compiled sporting appreciation ever preserved.
The figures who have consistently claimed this acclaim surely warrant some closer inspection.

Sir Stanley Matthews was 41 when he won the first Ballon d’Or. / PRESSE SPORTS/IMAGOThe Ballon d’Or has gone through more format changes than the Argentinian top flight. When Sir Stanley Matthews was presented with the first edition’s trophy in Blackpool’s club house in 1956, only 16 judges had a vote. The 2026 prize will be decided by a century of journalists from each of the top 100 ranked FIFA nations.

Matthews won the prize with 47 points in 1956. In 2025, 47 points would only have been good enough for 18th place, narrowly ahead of Scott McTominay. No player should be penalized by the system France Football happened to be operating at the time of their consideration, so all votes have been normalized.

Rather than adding up each player’s raw points total, their votes have been expressed as a proportion of the total score they could have achieved. Take Matthews as the example: there were 16 jurors in 1956 who listed their top five; first place got five points, second received four points, third got three and so on. In the scenario where every voter picked the same winner, they could only get a maximum of 80 points (16 lots of five points).

So, Matthews’s normalized score for 1956 is his actual tally (47) divided by the maximum based on that year’s system (80) multiplied by 100 so that we’re working with nice big numbers, which equates to 58.8.
Normalized points = (total score ÷ best score possible) x 100

The RSSSF dutifully compiled a complete breakdown of the Ballon d’Or votes for every year between its inception in 1956 and 2009 before France Football began its collaboration with FIFA. The diligence of their record-keeping cannot be lauded enough. FIFA’s archives helpfully contained a full list of votes between 2010 and 2015 while each edition of France Football belatedly published the winners’ points tallies from 2016 onward.

Span: 1992–2000Nation: NetherlandsNominations: 6Wins: 0Podiums: 2Normalized Points: 125For Dennis Bergkamp, time is a malleable concept. The best always know what pass they are going to play before the ball comes to them but Bergkamp claimed to know the exact movements of the 21 other players on the field in advance.“I always had a picture in my head of how it would be in three seconds or two seconds,” Arsenal’s ‘Ice Man’ explained in his accurately entitled autobiography Stillness and Speed. “I could calculate it, or sense it. I’d think: ‘He’s moving this way, and he’s moving that way, so if I give the pass with that pace neither of them can touch it because they are moving away from my line.’”

Kaká was a worthy winner in 2007. / PIERRE VERDY/AFP/Getty ImagesSpan: 2004–2009Nation: BrazilNominations: 6Wins: 1 (2007)Podiums: 1Normalized Points: 125“This is a new era of football, a new cycle is starting,” Kaká declared after winning the 2007 Ballon d’Or with Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi in second and third respectively. “There were great players before, but now the new players are starting to make history.”The rakish Brazilian may have included himself in that future roll call of honors but he would never again scale those same heights, watching on instead while Ronaldo and Messi dominated all before them.Yet, to fail in comparison to such figures is no denigration at all. Kaká was a mesmeric force in his own distinct era, boasting the technical artistry of yesteryear’s great No. 10s with a modern dynamism. The man who won the Ballon d’Or the year before him, Fabio Cannavaro, summed it up: “It was beautiful to watch him play.”
Erling Haaland you are built different. pic.twitter.com/rDmbDDzoOM

Span: 2021–2026Nation: NorwayNominations: 6Wins: 0Podiums: 1Normalized Points: 127As a precocious 19-year-old, Erling Haaland admitted that he aspired to the ultimate individual recognition. “That’s the dream yes,” he confirmed, “but a dream I share with a million other young players in the world.” Haaland is very much that one in a million.A striker with the relentless goal record to match his maniacal worth ethic off the field was routinely categorized as “a robot.” Shortly after Haaland led Manchester City to the European treble in 2023 with a frankly ludicrous 52 goals in 53 games, Gazzetta dello Sport ranked Victor Osimhen as “the best of the human No. 9s” in Europe. Haaland didn’t count.That year Haaland lost out in the Ballon d’Or to another alien, Lionel Messi, but was quite content with any type of honor he received.“My father always said it doesn’t matter which trophy or recognition you get,” he explained, “you should always appreciate someone appreciating what you do. He knocked this into my head.”

Karim Benzema won his Ballon d’Or in 2022. / IMAGO/Xinhua  Span: 2008–2023Nation: FranceNominations: 12Wins: 1 (2022)Podiums: 1Normalized Points: 127Karim Benzema had three ambitions in life when he set out on his career in professional soccer; buy his mother a house, join Real Madrid and win the Ballon d’Or. Tick, tick, tick.Cristiano Ronaldo’s perennial sidekick blossomed into Madrid’s undisputed hero once the Portuguese phenom took his roadshow to Turin. While he had to do Ronaldo’s running, Benzema only cracked 30 goals in one of his first nine seasons at Madrid. Without that weight on his shoulders, the languid French star hit the 30-mark in four of his next five campaigns.“People talk about Karim as a pure No. 9, a 9 and a half, a 10; for me, he’s a bit of everything,” Zinédine Zidane once gushed about his compatriot. “I would define him as a total footballer.”

Gigi Riva had a shot likened to the clap of thunder. / HUM Images/Universal Images Group/Getty ImagesSpan: 1967–1970Nation: ItalyNominations: 4Wins: 0Podiums: 2Normalized Points: 132The vote for the 1969 Ballon d’Or winner was so close France Football decided to honor the two players who could only be separated by four points at the same time. Gianni Rivera would narrowly claim the gong ahead of Gigi Riva, yet it was Cagliari’s prolific striker who ended the day triumphantly.The paper’s editor-in-chief, Max Urbini, had traveled to San Siro for Milan’s clash with Cagliari to hand out the Ballon d’Or four months after the vote. Despite coming out second best to the Rossoneri’s skipper in an individual sense, Riva would lead the Sardinians to the club’s first (and so far only) league title that month.
